label: Conflicting
claim: The coronavirus is spreading so fast that it will infect 70% of humanity in 2020.
doc: COVID-19 projections varied significantly and were based on scenarios where the virus was not controlled. To address the pandemic, countries introduced various containment measures including lockdowns of towns and cities, bans on large gatherings, and restrictions on travellers from hard-hit areas such as China, Italy, and Iran. Additionally, major sporting events, carnivals, and other events were postponed or cancelled. These interventions were implemented globally, where the world's estimated population in 2020 was around 7.6 billion people.
speaker: Facts Verse

label: Conflicting
claim: US Senator Amy Klobuchar said While we are all sitting here debating, Wisconsin has kicked hundreds of thousands of people off of their voting rolls
doc: In 2021, the Wisconsin Elections Commission sent letters to 234,000 voters whom it believed may have moved, instructing them to update their voter registrations with new addresses or notify the commission if they had not moved. Those who did not act on the letters would have their voter registrations suspended after April 2021. However, a Wisconsin appeals court struck down an Ozaukee County judge's ruling that thousands of people be quickly removed from the state's voter rolls because they were believed to have moved. The appeals judges also unanimously overturned a finding that state election officials were in contempt of court for not removing people from the rolls, and instead ruled that voters targeted for purge would remain on the rolls.
speaker: Amy Klobuchar

label: Conflicting
claim: Government is actively involved in the property sector, having provided more than 4 million houses since 1994.
doc: A claim made on February 13, 2020, regarding South Africa reported that the South African Government had delivered 3,030,824 housing units from 1994/1995 to 2015/16. Subsequently, 90,692 houses were built in the 2016/17 financial year, followed by 86,048 in 2017/18, and 77,584 in 2018/19. When all years between 1994 and 2020 are combined, the total reaches 3,285,148 housing units. However, these figures from the Department of Human Settlements do not include what is called "serviced sites," which are sites that have the potential to become homes but are not yet developed. Housing units and serviced sites are counted separately in the housing data. When serviced sites are included in the total housing numbers provided by the government, the figure rises to 4.7 million. Professor Aly Karam has raised concerns about these statistics, warning that the Department of Human Settlements' housing statistics "have not been independently verified and should be read with caution, as indicative rather than entirely conclusive."
speaker: Jacob Zuma

label: Conflicting
claim: Gov. Tony Evers wants to release half of the prison population."
doc: Tony Evers has long expressed his desire to address overcrowding in Wisconsin's prison system, though he and his administration have emphasized the need to proceed carefully and gradually. During the 2018 campaign, Evers told the Milwaukee Journal Sentinel he would consider releasing some inmates early, overhauling truth-in-sentencing, and treating 17-year-olds as juveniles instead of adults in criminal proceedings, among other reform policies. During a Democratic debate, he stated that cutting the prison population in half is "a goal that's worth accomplishing." As State Schools Superintendent, Evers indicated that Wisconsin should follow the example of states like Texas that have cut parole revocations and expanded drug courts. His proposed measures include considering the early release of some inmates, providing more drug treatment behind bars, treating 17-year-olds as juveniles rather than adults for criminal charges, and overhauling truth-in-sentencing to allow prisoners to be released for good behavior. He emphasized his position by noting, "The fact that we as a state spend more on corrections than (the University of Wisconsin) System tells me the last thing we need is to build a brand-new prison." However, while he expressed these goals, he did not specify an exact number of prisoners he intended to release.
speaker: Robin Vos

label: Conflicting
claim:
US Rep Mark Pocan stated on January 16, 2020 in a tweet:
“There’s an Amazon distribution center that was advertising, last time I was there, up to $12.75 an hour. Your parents made that three decades ago.”
doc: When adjusted for inflation, the average hourly wage in the United States today possesses roughly equivalent purchasing power to what it held in 1978, following a significant decline during the 1980s and early 1990s, succeeded by inconsistent and uneven growth thereafter. While Representative Mark Pocan's assertion that an offer of $12.75 equates to hourly wages from 30 years prior—whether viewed as a direct comparison or with inflation considered—is not precise from a strict perspective, his broader argument about wage stagnation holds merit. The average wage in the 1990s was $10.43, illustrating the broader trend of limited wage growth over recent decades.
speaker: Rep Mark Pocan

label: Conflicting
claim: U.S President Donald Trump's transportation secretary, Elaine Chao, sent a 97 million dollar contract to help her husband, Mitch McConnell's re-election bid.
doc: On June 8, 2018, U.S. Senate Majority Leader Mitch McConnell, the Senator of Kentucky, announced that the U.S. Department of Transportation awarded a $67.4 million federal grant to the Kentucky Transportation Cabinet to fund improvements to Interstate 75 and Interstate 71 in Boone County as part of President Donald Trump's pledge to rebuild America's infrastructure. The grant was designated to rebuild two I-75/I-71 interchanges in Boone County. On August 6, 2018, McConnell formally announced his plans to seek a seventh term, speaking at a Republican breakfast in western Kentucky ahead of the Fancy Farm picnic, stating "I'm going to be running for re-election in 2020. I don't like starting late." Days after launching his 2020 reelection campaign, McConnell asked Owensboro's mayor to set up a luncheon with business and political leaders at which the senator claimed credit for delivering the grant. The grant was tied to McConnell's re-election through Transportation Secretary Elaine Chao's designation of an intermediary for Kentucky—a privilege other states did not enjoy—which gave special advantage to projects favored by her husband, potentially benefiting his political interests. By December 29, 2019, ethicists and scholars noted that such arrangements, where a Cabinet secretary takes actions to help her husband get reelected, could be perceived as corruption or "swamp behavior."
speaker: Farron Cousins
reporting_source: Ring of Fire Show on YouTube

label: Conflicting
claim: Prime Minister Modi’s government has not mentioned the National Record of Citizenship (NRC) since his government came to power in 2014 and any implementation of the NRC was limited only to Assam post the Supreme Court directive.
doc: Narendra Modi became prime minister of India on May 20, 2014. Since assuming office, Modi's government has undertaken the National Record of Citizenship (NRC), an exercise conducted in Assam between February 2015 and August 2019. While India's home minister Amit Shah has hinted at the possibility of a nationwide NRC, the government has not extended the National Record of Citizenship to any areas in India other than Assam. Although the government may have mentioned the NRC since 2014, it has not made changes or suggested extending the scheme beyond Assam.
speaker: Narendra Modi

label: Conflicting
claim: Russian Authorities are not moving toward closing off the Russian internet from the global internet using the "Sovereign Internet law" which came into effect on November 1st 2019.
doc: The Russian Sovereign Internet law requires internet service providers to install network equipment known as deep packet inspection (DPI), capable of identifying the source of traffic and filtering content. This will allow the country's telecommunications watchdog Roskomnadzor to be more effective at blocking sites. The law gives the Kremlin the possibility to switch off connections within Russia or completely to the worldwide web "in an emergency," with the government deciding what constitutes a threat and what actions should be taken. Russia is seeking to route the country's web traffic and data through state-controlled points, reducing reliance on foreign servers over which it has less control. The law, which was signed by President Vladimir Putin earlier this year, allows the government to block content without judicial consent and leaves users unaware about what information is being blocked and why. Campaigners say it is an attempt to increase censorship, building on internet legislation that already curtails freedom of expression and privacy. According to Rachel Denber, Human Rights Watch's deputy Europe and Central Asia director, "Now the government can directly censor content or even turn Russia's internet into a closed system without telling the public what they are doing or why." Christian Mihr from Reporters Without Borders stated that the law "proves that the Russian leadership is ready to bring the entire network infrastructure under political control in order to cut off the digital information flow whenever needed." As a test, the Russian government cut off a part of the access to the global internet after the law came into place.
speaker: Vladimir Putin

label: Conflicting
claim: There's a titanic battle between American nationalism and American liberal globalism. Donald Trump embodies the first camp, and half of the Americans support him on this issue, believing that the U.S. spends too much [in terms of] manpower and resources on foreign policy.
doc: A significant majority of Americans, 69%, believe that the USA spends too much manpower and resources on foreign policy. Despite this concern, 77% of Americans say that NATO membership is good for the USA. Trump represents American nationalism through his desire to withdraw from NATO, motivated by his belief that other countries are not spending enough of their GDP on defense. However, the battle for a pro-NATO bill was not titanic, as the bill was passed unanimously by both Republicans and Democrats.
speaker: Vladimir Batyuk

label: Conflicting
claim: In US "160 million people like their private insurance."
doc:
Survey data reveals a complex picture of American attitudes toward healthcare. While most people with employer-sponsored insurance are generally satisfied with their health plans, with large shares reporting they feel "grateful" and "content" about their insurance and fewer expressing anger or frustration, significant financial challenges persist. Four in ten Americans report that their family has experienced problems paying medical bills or difficulty affording premiums or out-of-pocket medical costs. About half say someone in their household skipped or postponed some type of medical care or prescription drugs in the past year due to cost, and seventeen percent say they have had to make difficult sacrifices to pay healthcare or insurance costs. A Gallup poll conducted in January 2019 found that 70 percent of Americans describe the current U.S. healthcare system as being in a state of crisis or having major problems.

In 2017, approximately 156 million people had employer-based coverage, representing almost half the total U.S. population and 60 percent of non-elderly adults. However, among those with employer-sponsored insurance, 28 percent of U.S. adults were underinsured in 2018. Of the approximately 193.9 million U.S. adults ages 19 to 64 in 2018, the underinsurance problem extended beyond the employer-sponsored sector, with 42 percent of people who bought private plans on their own reporting a lack of adequate coverage in 2018.
speaker: Joe Biden

label: Conflicting
claim: (Nigeria has an estimated physician-patient ratio of one doctor to every 4,000 to 5,000 patients.) ...[This is] six times smaller than the physician-patient ratio (one physician to every 600 doctors) recommended by WHO.
doc: In Nigeria, 40,000 doctors provide care for a population of 200 million people, resulting in an estimated physician-patient ratio of between 1:4,800 and 1:5,000. The World Health Organisation has not prescribed any ideal ratio of healthcare workers to population.
speaker: Socrates Mbamalu

label: Conflicting
claim: 1 in 6 in the US get food poisoning each year but only 1 in 66 in the UK.
doc: The estimate that one in 66 people in the UK gets food poisoning is based on a 2011 FSA report, which estimated that in the UK a million people a year suffer a foodborne illness. With the UK's population at 66,435,600 in 2018, the original claimant appears to have derived the one in 66 figure by dividing the total population by the number of cases. However, this is not an accurate statistic. In contrast, the figure of one in six for the US comes from the Center for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), which estimates that each year roughly one in six Americans, or approximately 48 million people, get sick as a result of foodborne diseases. The CDC confirmed this came from a paper published in 2011 and stated that the estimates represent a fairly accurate representation of the burden of foodborne diseases in the US, given the US population in 2018 was 332,140,037. Despite these figures, the data between the two countries is not comparable and varies considerably in how and when it was collected. There are significant differences in the methodology behind the estimates, and real-world factors such as access to medical care, which differs widely between the two countries, can also affect the comparison. This claim was made on 06/10/2019.
speaker: Jolyon Maugham QC

label: Conflicting
claim: PM Modi announced a child helpline (1098) for the benefit of children in various crisis situations.
doc: CHILDLINE 1098 is a 24-hour, 365-day-a-year free emergency phone service for children in need of aid and assistance. The helpline was started nearly two decades ago as a field action project of the Department of Family and Child Welfare at the Tata Institute of Social Sciences (TISS). CHILDLINE India Foundation was formed in 1999 and subsequently granted exclusive 'Nodal Mother NGO' status in 2006-07 by the Ministry of Woman and Child Development, authorizing it to establish CHILDLINE services throughout the country.

label: Conflicting
claim: Paul Manafort case recovers between forty two and forty six million U.S dollars meaning the cost to taxpayers approaches zero in investigation into Russian interference in the 2016 U.S election.
doc: Robert Mueller's special counsel investigation into Russian interference in the 2016 U.S. election cost nearly $32 million in total, as reported in the Justice Department's filing of the special counsel's fourth and final expenditures. However, the investigation resulted in significant financial recoveries through the plea deal with Paul Manafort, who agreed to forfeit real estate and cash estimated to be worth between $42 million and $46 million. Although a Justice Department official stated that the recovered money would not go directly to funding the Russia investigation, according to Congressman Jerrold Nadler, the cost to the U.S. taxpayer approaches zero as a result of the $42 million recovered by Mueller.
speaker: Jerry Nadler

label: Conflicting
claim: Trump claims his deregulatory actions are saving American households $3,000 a year.
doc: Trump derived the $3,000 annual saving figure from "The Economic Effects of Federal Deregulation since January 2017: An Interim Report" published by The Council of Economic Advisers in June 2019. According to this report, the Council of Economic Advisers estimates that after 5 to 10 years, the new approach to Federal regulation will have raised real incomes by $3,100 per household per year. However, the figures presented in the report are estimates and have been refuted by numerous sources, including the Office of Management and Budget, which argued that the Stream Protection Rule had less effect than the CEA claimed. Additionally, the projected $3,100 increase in household income is not immediate but rather would be realized only after a period of 5 to 10 years.
speaker: Donald Trump

label: Conflicting
claim: One in four South African employees have been diagnosed with depression.
doc: Depression is one of the most common mental disorders in South Africa, with an estimated 9·8% lifetime prevalence for major depressive disorder in adults. A 2016 study examining depression in South African employees found that one in four workers reported depression; however, this study was limited to employees who worked in advertising or market research, and therefore cannot be generalized to workforces in South Africa as a whole. The study had several significant limitations. The results relied entirely on subjective responses to an online questionnaire, and while anonymity supports the reliability of the data, the study design did not allow for diagnosis of depression to be verified. Additionally, the sample size, although in line with a previous study using the IDEA instrument, may still have not been large enough to give clearer results on the impact of absenteeism in the workplace in South Africa. The study was also limited by recall bias, as participants may have experienced difficulties accurately remembering events or experiences from the past.
speaker: Fin24

label: Conflicting
claim: 83% of the benefits from the Republican tax law go to the top 1% of income earners in the United States.
doc: According to December 2017 estimates from the Tax Policy Center, the distribution of tax cut benefits from the Tax Cuts Act would vary significantly over time. In 2018, the top 1% of income earners would receive 20.5% of the tax cut benefits, with projections increasing to 25.3% by 2025. By 2027, the top 1% share would rise dramatically to 82.8% of the tax cut benefits. This substantial shift in benefits distribution results from a key policy provision in the Senate Republican tax law overhaul: individual tax cuts are set to expire within 10 years, while corporate tax cuts remain permanent. This expiration of individual tax provisions causes a higher percentage of tax benefits to accrue to the top 1% in later years. However, Senate Republicans indicated that their intention was for Congress to extend these individual tax cuts beyond the 10-year period, and they argued that the effect of this scheduled expiration should not be included in analysis of the bill.
speaker: Bernie Sanders
reporting_source: Night two of the primary election debates

label: Conflicting
claim: Many of America's 2.3 million prisoners are incarcerated for nonviolent drug crimes
doc: The United States prison population stands at 2,121,600 individuals. At a minimum, 55 percent of those in state prison have been convicted of a violent crime, and more than half of these violent offenders, or nearly 30 percent of the total prison population, have been found guilty of murder, manslaughter, rape, or sexual assault according to the Bureau of Justice Statistics. Slightly less than 15 percent are incarcerated for drug crimes, despite most Americans believing the figure to be approximately 50 percent. While drugs play a more significant role in the federal prison system, the federal system holds only about 10 percent of all prisoners, with most incarcerated people housed in state prisons.
speaker: Beto O'Rourke

label: Conflicting
claim: President Donald Trump has thrown 32 million people off their health care that they have.
doc: In 2017, the Congressional Budget Office estimated that the Obamacare Repeal Reconciliation Act of 2017 would increase the number of uninsured by 32 million people over 10 years. However, not all of these people would likely be thrown off their insurance. Donald Trump did plan a bill that would throw people off their health plans. The Affordable Care Act, by contrast, aimed to extend health coverage to uninsured Americans, who were estimated at the time the bill was passed to number around 47 million.
speaker: Bernie Sanders
reporting_source: Night two of the primary election debates

label: Conflicting
claim: Number one reason for why American families go broke is the cost of healthcare
doc: The relationship between medical debt and personal bankruptcy in the United States is more complex than commonly assumed. While more than a quarter of U.S. adults struggle to pay their medical bills, and an estimated 40% of Americans racked up debt resulting from a medical issue in 2014, the causal link between medical debt and bankruptcy is not straightforward. According to a 2014 report from the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau, about 20% of Americans have substantial medical debt, yet in a given year less than 1% of Americans file for personal bankruptcy, suggesting that many people face medical debt without going bankrupt. A 2018 study published in the New England Journal of Medicine found that while hospital costs had an impact on bankruptcy, they were frequently just one of many contributing factors. Researchers noted that "medical factors play a much smaller role in causing U.S. bankruptcies than has previously been claimed" and cautioned that "overemphasizing 'medical bankruptcies' may distract from understanding the true nature of economic hardship arising from high-cost health problems." The existing evidence on medical bankruptcy has been built on the fallacy that when two things occur together there is necessarily a causal relationship between them. Common causes of bankruptcy in the United States include divorce, expensive medical bills caused by disability or illness, poor financial management related to student loans and major purchases, reduced income or job loss, and unexpected emergencies. Three-quarters of people with a medically-related bankruptcy had health insurance, indicating that insurance coverage does not necessarily prevent financial hardship from medical costs.
speaker: Elizabeth Warren

label: Conflicting
claim: The US-Iran nuclear deal pushed back a nuclear breakout by 10–20 years.
doc: The Iran nuclear deal, known as the Joint Comprehensive Plan of Action, effectively shuts Iran's pathways to nuclear weapons while preserving its legal right to civilian nuclear energy. The deal cuts off all of Iran's pathways to a nuclear weapon, including a covert pathway, and puts in place vigorous, intrusive, and unprecedented transparency measures necessary to verify that Iran cannot pursue a weapon. It substantially lengthens the time Iran would need to enrich enough uranium for nuclear weapons, putting eyes on the program to detect any activity toward overt weaponization and drastically increasing the chance of detecting any so-called secret "sneakout." The deal extends the time Iran would need to produce an atomic bomb from two or three months to at least one year, which would give the United States and its allies an opportunity to react if the Iranians broke the agreement. Under these limits, "breakout time" at Natanz over the next decade would be extended to roughly a year, from the current estimated breakout time of 2 to 3 months. From year 11 to year 15, breakout time at Natanz will decline as Iran is permitted to replace its first-generation centrifuges with limited numbers of advanced models, although the restrictions on enriched uranium stocks and enrichment level continue through year 15. The deal puts strong, verifiable limits on Iran's ability to develop a nuclear weapon for at least the next 10 to 15 years and is potentially one of the most consequential accords in recent diplomatic history. The agreement also ensures sanctions can be snapped back into place if Iran violates the deal. After 15 years, all physical constraints on enrichment imposed by the agreement will be lifted, at which point Iran could build an enrichment plant large enough to produce low-enriched uranium to fuel a nuclear power reactor within a matter of years.
speaker: Cory Booker

label: Conflicting
claim: About 30% of LGBTQ kids do not go to school because of fear.
doc:
The Iran nuclear deal, according to proponents like Cory Booker, provided crucial transparency into Iran's nuclear program and pushed back a nuclear breakout by 10-20 years before the United States withdrew from the agreement. Regarding economic conditions, claims that the bottom 60% of American households are not receiving raises are incorrect. According to a 2018 Congressional Budget Office report, the bottom 60% saw their household income rise by 32% adjusted for inflation from 1979 to 2015, while the top 1% experienced a 233% increase over the same period.

On healthcare administration costs, Booker's assertion that private insurance overhead is 15 percent while Medicare's is only 2 percent is substantially accurate. Medicare's total administrative expenses were $9.9 billion, representing 1.3 percent of total Medicare expenditures—even lower than the 2 percent figure cited. However, the comparison is more nuanced than a simple comparison would suggest, as Medicare does spend less on administration than private insurers.

Regarding gun violence prevention, Connecticut's permit-to-purchase law passed in 1995 was associated with a 40% reduction in firearm homicide rates during the first 10 years of implementation and a 15.4% reduction in suicide rates, according to studies published in the American Journal of Public Health and Preventive Medicine in 2015.

Contrary to Beto O'Rourke's claim, Purdue Pharma has faced significant consequences related to the opioid crisis. In 2007, the company and three executives pleaded guilty to misbranding OxyContin and paid over $634 million in fines and other payments. Additionally, in March, Oklahoma's Attorney General reached a $270 million settlement with Purdue Pharma following allegations that the company contributed to the state's opioid epidemic.

On LGBTQ student safety, while Booker cited approximately 30% of LGBTQ students missing school due to fear, data shows more specific figures. The CDC found that 12.5% of LGB students missed school because they felt unsafe, compared to 5.6% of all students. However, the 2017 GLSEN National School Climate Survey, which included 23,001 lesbian, gay, bisexual, transgender and queer students aged 13-21 from all 50 states, D.C., and U.S. territories, found that 35% of LGBTQ students missed at least one day of school in the prior month due to feeling unsafe.
speaker: Cory Booker

label: Conflicting
claim: Sen. Cory Booker claimed the Iran nuclear deal “pushed back a nuclear breakout 10, 20 years.” during the 2020 U.S presidential debate
doc: The Iran nuclear deal, formally known as the Joint Comprehensive Plan of Action (JCPOA), was designed to cut off all of Iran's pathways to a nuclear weapon, including covert pathways, while implementing vigorous, intrusive, and unprecedented transparency measures to verify Iran's compliance. According to Sen. Cory Booker, the agreement "pushed back a nuclear breakout 10, 20 years." Specifically, the deal extended the time Iran would need to produce an atomic bomb from two or three months to at least one year for a minimum of 10 years, which would give the United States and its allies an opportunity to react if Iran broke the agreement. For the first 15 years under the JCPOA, all enrichment would be limited to Natanz, making Iran's nuclear program vulnerable to military attack and rendering swift detection of any breakout attempt likely, thereby creating a high risk of provoking military intervention. Some contributors believe that by year 15, breakout time could be comparable to current levels of a few months, while others contend it could be reduced to a few weeks. Iran would be unlikely to attempt breakout at Natanz during this period due to the certainty of detection and the substantial military risk. The agreement also ensured that sanctions could be snapped back into place if Iran violated the deal, and the physical constraints on enrichment imposed by the agreement would eventually be lifted.

label: Conflicting
claim: Sen. Cory Booker claimed private insurance overhead was 15 percent, while Medicare’s was “only at 2 percent.”
doc: In 2018, Medicare's administrative expenses totaled $9.9 billion, representing 1.3 percent of total Medicare expenditures for the year. This figure is even lower than the 2 percent figure cited by Senator Cory Booker. When comparing administrative expenses between public Medicare and private Medicare, the administrative expenses percentage of benefits for the public system is significantly lower than private alternatives. However, the definitions of administrative expenses are incompatible and not reconcilable between the two systems, making direct comparisons problematic. There are additional reasons why these numbers are not comparable. When examining broader financial data, per-member income and benefits are larger for public Medicare and have grown faster than Medicare Part C, representing a reversal of earlier trends. Furthermore, public Medicare faces solvency challenges in many years, whereas private Medicare insurers maintain an 85% loss ratio.

label: Conflicting
claim: 1.9 million more children are in good and outstanding schools.
doc: The claim refers to schools in England, U.K., where the Office for Standards in Education, Children's Services and Skills (Ofsted) inspects and regulates services that care for children and young people and services that provide education and skills for learners of all ages. According to official figures, 1.9 million children attend a school rated good or outstanding by Ofsted in the U.K. However, this statistic does not account for 580,000 pupils who were in schools that hadn't even been inspected since 2010. While the 1.9 million figure is factually accurate, it fails an important test of any statistic—it does not show the user what the producer believes it shows. In this case, it does not adequately demonstrate that standards in schools have improved since 2010, at least not to the extent that a quarter of all pupils are in significantly better schools because of any policy intervention.
speaker: Michael Gove

label: Conflicting
claim: It costs £8 per day to watch TV in hospital if you’re 82.
doc: Hospitals obtain TV systems from companies such as HTS or Hospedia, with Hospedia providing free TV services. However, the cost of watching TV in hospitals varies by institution. At the County Durham and Darlington NHS Trust as of April 2018, TV was free on channels one to five in the mornings, while paid packages ranged from £7.90 per day for the "1 Day TV Bundle" to £24.90 per day for the "3 Day TV & Movies Bundle." Some hospitals, including James Paget University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust, provide TV free of charge on certain wards.
speaker: Kelly Jenkinson

label: Conflicting
claim: Being vegan for a year saves 365 animals.
doc: According to various sources, adopting a vegan diet saves a significant number of animals annually. The Vegan Society estimates that 37 animals per year would be saved, comprising 1 pig, 16 fish, 19 birds, and 1 laying hen. PETA conducted a study with a higher estimate of 198 animals saved per year, broken down as 130 shellfish, 40 fish, 26 chickens, 1 turkey, half a pig, and one tenth of a cow. Vegancalculator.com provides another metric, estimating that 1 animal would be saved per day.
speaker: planetbasednews

label: Conflicting
claim: In the 2019 EU parliamentary election, the "total leave vote" was 57.8% and the "total remain vote" was 41.5%.
doc: In the EU parliamentary elections, leave votes received a total of 58% while remain votes obtained 41.5%. The Brexit Party contributed 31.6% of the total leave votes, while The Labour Party accounted for 14.1% of the leave votes cast.
speaker: Message from the People

label: Conflicting
claim: 12% of the electorate voted for no deal in the 2019 EU parliamentary elections
doc: Elections to the European Parliament take place every five years by universal adult suffrage to vote European parliament members. In the 2019 EU parliamentary elections in Great Britain, two parties supported a no-deal Brexit as their preferred outcome: the Brexit Party and UKIP. A no-deal Brexit, also known as a clean break Brexit, was the potential withdrawal of the UK from the European Union without a withdrawal agreement. These two parties won 35% of the vote in Great Britain between them, with the Brexit Party receiving 31.6% and UKIP receiving 3.3%. This meant that 34% of all UK voters who voted in the EU parliamentary elections voted for a party that seemed to favour no deal, representing about 13% of the total UK electorate. However, not all those who voted for a no-deal party necessarily preferred a no-deal Brexit. A poll by Lord Ashcroft taken just after the election found that 67% of those reporting they had voted for the Brexit Party said they thought the best Brexit outcome would be leaving the EU with no deal, while 23% thought the best outcome would be some form of deal, but not the one negotiated by the government. Northern Ireland elections use the Single Transferable Vote system, under which voters rank candidates in order of preference by marking 1, 2, 3 and so on next to the names of candidates on a ballot paper, and can rank as many or as few candidates as they like or vote for just one candidate.
speaker: Anna Soubry

label: Conflicting
claim: Joe Biden told Ukrainian government leaders that if they did not sack the prosecutor going after his son then they would not give them a $2 billion loan.
doc: Since May 7, 2014, the Ukrainian government's General Prosecutor's Office has been investigating case No. 42014000000000375 of alleged criminal activity of subsidiaries of Burisma Holdings in Ukraine. Prosecutor General Viktor Shokin served as the lead investigator in this matter. Burisma Holdings employed Vice President Joe Biden's younger son, Hunter Biden, as a board member. Biden's office was quoted on the record acknowledging Hunter Biden's role at Burisma in a New York Times article about the general prosecutor's Burisma case that appeared four months before Biden took action. The vice president's office suggested in that article that Hunter Biden was a lawyer free to pursue his own private business deals. In March 2016, Vice President Joe Biden threatened Ukrainian President Petro Poroshenko that the Obama administration would pull $1 billion in U.S. loan guarantees if the Ukrainian government did not fire Prosecutor General Viktor Shokin, who was investigating the company employing his son.
speaker: Donald Trump

label: Conflicting
claim: Since 2011, there has been documentation of 1,671 dead bodies recovered in Texas, many in Brooks County on the US Mexico border.
doc: Official figures of deaths are published by the US Government. In 2012, Texas surpassed Arizona in border deaths, with the majority occurring in the Rio Grande Valley and more specifically in Brooks County, Texas. While no comprehensive estimates exist on the total number of injuries or deaths that occur along the border, as of April 15, 2011, 145 bodies had been recovered in the graves, as families throughout Mexico await news on whether their loved ones are among the dead.
speaker: Dan Patrick (Lieutenant Governor of Texas)

label: Conflicting
claim: Since Trump took office, 7 million more people lack health insurance that used to have it.
doc: Between 2008 and 2018, the rate of uninsured U.S. adults fluctuated significantly. In 2016, the uninsured rate reached its lowest point at 10.9% of U.S. adults. However, the situation deteriorated in subsequent years, with the uninsured rate rising to 12.2% by December 12, 2017, and further increasing to 13.7% in 2018, when seven million adults lost health insurance coverage. Multiple reports documented this rising trend of Americans without insurance during this period.
speaker: Bernie Sanders

label: Conflicting
claim: In the Republican tax bill, 83% of the benefits went to the top 1%.
doc: Under the 2017 Tax Cuts and Jobs Act, the distribution of benefits was complex and shifted over time. While the top 5 percent received the most substantial benefits by far, in the early years approximately half of the tax breaks went to the bottom 90 percent of taxpayers. However, the picture skewed increasingly toward the wealthiest in later years. The benefits of the law were heavily concentrated among upper-middle and upper-class Americans, with nearly two-thirds of the benefit going to the richest fifth of Americans in 2018. The tax cuts were primarily aimed at corporate rate reductions, which mostly benefited Americans rich enough to own stock. Since lower earners derived minimal benefit from corporate tax cuts, by 2027 poor and middle-class Americans would see a very mild tax increase on average.
speaker: Bernie Sanders

label: Conflicting
claim: Since Trump took office, 7 million more people lack health insurance that used to have it.
doc: According to the January 2019 Gallup estimate, insurance coverage declined by 2.8 percentage points from its low in 2016. Gallup converted this rise into 7 million people who lost insurance in 2019. This figure contrasts with the government survey, which reported about 1.3 million people lost insurance during the same period.
speaker: Bernie Sanders

label: Conflicting
claim: The Kenyan Government asked six ministers to step aside in its last term in 2015.
doc: In 2015, members of the Kenyan Government were asked to step aside. Several ministers were suspended, and multiple members complied by stepping aside from their positions. Five individuals were removed from the Cabinet, and additional members left the government as well.
speaker: Kenyan deputy president William Ruto

label: Conflicting
claim: Kenyan deputy president William Ruto asked six ministers in the last term (2015 to 2019) to step aside.
doc: During the 2015-19 term of office, several changes occurred within Kenya's government. Kenyan ministers were asked to step aside, government officials were suspended, and other government officials left government.
speaker: William Ruto

label: Conflicting
claim: In 2018, provisional estimates show the Kenya economy grew by 6.1%.
doc: Provisional estimates in 2018 indicated that the Kenyan economy had grown by 6.1% in the year to September, based on future growth projections of 6.4% for the full year and existing figures showing the economy grew 5.8% in the first three months of 2018, 6.2% in the second quarter, and 6% in the third quarter of the year.
speaker: Uhuru Kenyatta, C.G.H., President Of The Republic Of Kenya

label: Conflicting
claim: In 2018, provisional estimates show the Kenyan economy grew by 6.1%.
doc: Kenya's economy demonstrated provisional growth estimates of 6.0 per cent during the third quarter of 2018, with overall economic growth reaching 5.7% for the full year 2018, supported by a predicted growth rate of 5.8%. The Kenyan economy has been on a steady recovery path, though this growth should be interpreted with caution. Historically, Kenya's economic growth rate has averaged 5–6% over the past decade, implying challenges in the country's productive capacity. A 2018 study by the PBO established that Kenya's potential output is at 5% on average, suggesting that the country's economic performance may have peaked in the past decade. With actual economic growth coalescing at approximately the same level as potential GDP, achieving significantly higher growth will require substantial changes in policy direction and budget execution to scale up the country's productive capacity. Unless such changes occur, it will be difficult for the economy to achieve a growth rate significantly higher than 6%, despite policy documents targeting a higher economic growth of 7–10%.
speaker: Uhuru Kenyatta

label: Conflicting
claim: more than 50 lakh pregnant women expected to benefit every year with cash incentive of 6000 rupees
doc: The Indian Government administers the Pradhan Mantri Matru Vandana Yojana (PMMVY), a maternity benefit scheme designed to provide cash incentives to eligible pregnant women. Under this scheme, Rs. 5,000 are provided to eligible beneficiaries in three installments. Additionally, eligible beneficiaries receive the remaining cash incentive as per approved norms towards maternity benefit under the Janani Suraksha Yojana (JSY) following institutional delivery, bringing the total average cash incentive to Rs. 6,000 per woman. As of the data available, 46 lakh women (46,54,956) have received this payment through the program, rather than the initially projected 50 lakh women annually.
speaker: Ministry of Health & Family Welfare (MoHFW), Government of India

label: Conflicting
claim: President Donald Trump wants to change the  Affordable Care Act (ACA) protections, abolishing health insurance for kids who are 26 years of age or younger who are currently on their parents plans, which will throw 32 million Americans off their current health insurance.
doc: Trump sought to have the federal courts find the ACA unconstitutional and nullify the entire law. Should the ACA be removed, his administration would plan to offer an unspecified alternative at a later date. The 32 million figure cited comes from a Congressional Budget Office estimate of the impact of the Obamacare Repeal Reconciliation Act of 2017, which would have repealed the ACA altogether and replaced it with an unnamed replacement. According to the CBO, this plan would increase the number of uninsured by 32 million individuals over ten years. The number of uninsured would increase because in the nongroup market, some people would choose not to have insurance partly because they currently choose to be covered under existing law to avoid paying the penalty. Under the proposed legislation, without the mandate penalty, some people would forgo insurance in response to higher premiums that the CBO and Joint Committee on Taxation project would be charged. Insurers would still be required to provide coverage to any applicant and would not be able to vary premiums to reflect enrollees' health status or to limit coverage of preexisting medical conditions. Under the GOP health plan, young adults up to the age of 26 would be able to stay on their parents' insurance plans.
speaker: Bernie Sanders (Senator)

label: Conflicting
claim: People living in Labour councils pay on average £351 less council tax than those living in Tory councils.
doc: On 30th March 2019, a claim suggested that Labour councils charged £351 less in council tax than Tory councils. However, this calculation presents a significant issue: residents often pay council tax to more than one body, which may be run by different political parties, meaning that no single party is necessarily responsible for every penny paid. In 2019, the average council tax in councils with a majority Labour council was £1,168, compared to £1,519 in collecting councils with a majority Conservative council. It should be noted that councils do not set their own council tax for their elected areas.
speaker: The Labour party

label: Conflicting
claim: A double taxation avoidance agreement was signed between India and three new countries, which are: Mauritius, Cyprus, and Singapore.
doc: India has completed double taxation avoidance agreement renegotiations with 23 countries, including Switzerland, Mauritius, Cyprus, and Singapore. Mauritius signed its DTAA with India in 1983, Singapore on 24th January, 1994, and Cyprus on the 18th of November 2016.

label: Conflicting
claim: In the last two years The U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement officers have made 266,000 arrests of criminal aliens…including those charged or convicted of nearly 100,000 assaults, 30,000 sex crimes, 4,000 kidnappings, and 4,000 murders.
doc: Immigration and Customs Enforcement officers in the United States can charge a single person with multiple crimes and convictions. However, ICE does not account for individuals who have multiple convictions and criminal charges. Between 2016 and 2018, ICE officers made 266,109 arrests in the United States. It is important to note that a criminal charge does not mean a person is guilty of a crime. Regarding assault offenses specifically, ICE recorded 20,766 criminal charges and 29,987 criminal convictions in 2018, totaling 50,753 offenses. In 2017, ICE recorded 48,454 total assault offenses.
speaker: US President Donald Trump

label: Conflicting
claim: A generation ago, 37 cents out of every US food dollar went into a farmer’s pocket. Today, it’s 15 cents.
doc: The food dollar series measures annual expenditures by U.S. consumers on domestically produced food. According to a 2015 Congressional Research Service report that combined several data sets, the farm share of the food dollar was about 37 cents during the 1970-1980 period. In the current period, the farmers' share of the food dollar is 14.6 cents; however, under a metric measuring farm production's net receipt, farms receive only 7.8 cents of the dollar. The gap between 14.6 cents and 7.8 cents reflects that farms spent 6.8 cents of the money they earned to purchase products from other industry groups, as farms themselves purchase goods and services like any other consumer. Given the phrasing about how much of the agriculture dollars "went into a farmer's pocket," the lower figure of 7.8 cents may be more appropriate than 14.6 cents. Even this figure does not account for an additional 1.4 cents that must go to hire labor, making the amount actually going into "the farmer's pocket" even lower.
speaker: Elizabeth Warren

label: Conflicting
claim: Lagos has an estimated 21 million inhabitants
doc: While one population forecast estimated Lagos city's population in Nigeria at approximately 24,187,400 in 2019, there is no accurate or reliable figure available for the city's population during that year.

label: Conflicting
claim: 3,65,996 crore rupees were directly transferred into bank account of beneficiaries of PAHAL, India's Direct Benefit Transfer for LPG, 431consumer schemes
doc: In 2019, India's Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) system paid 2,61,71,50,93,600 rupees to PAHAL beneficiaries across 318 different schemes.
speaker: BJP government

label: Conflicting
claim: Medicare for All would result in massive tax increases like never before as well as the loss of private coverage for over 180 million Americans.
doc: Sanders' Medicare for All proposal would establish a single, national health insurance program covering everyone who lives in the United States. According to the bill introduced in 2017, it would pay for every medically necessary service, including routine doctor visits, surgery, mental health care, and prescription drugs, with dental and vision care included in the package. Long-term care such as nursing home and related services would be expanded under both Senate and House versions of the proposal. The government would set payment rates for services, drugs, and medical equipment, with the secretary of Health and Human Services determining a national budget for all covered services each year, with spending limited by that cap. For individuals, there would be no costs—no deductibles, copays, or coinsurance, with limited exceptions for some prescription drugs capped at $200 a year and possibly for long-term care. The program would replace all other insurance with limited exceptions such as cosmetic surgery, meaning employer-provided insurance, Medicaid, and Medicare would all be eliminated. To fund this program, Sanders proposed raising taxes on income over $250,000 to a 52 percent marginal rate on income over $10 million, along with suggesting a wealth tax on the top 0.1 percent of households. This would result in roughly 180 million Americans with private insurance seeing their plans canceled. Unlike the current Medicare program for Americans 65 and over who share costs, Sanders' Medicare for All would be much more generous, covering medical bills completely with no burden on patients and no need for Medigap insurance or Medicare Advantage.
speaker: Donald trump

label: Conflicting
claim: 50% of all new jobs in South Africa, in the past year, were created in the Western Cape.
doc: Between quarter 3 2017 and quarter 3 2018, the Western Cape created 95,000 jobs, representing 50.5% of job creation. In the subsequent period from quarter 4 2017 to quarter 4 2018, 29,000 jobs were created, accounting for 8.1% of job creation. The fourth quarter data was released on 12 February 2019, followed by the manifesto release on 23 February 2019. The DA opted to use the older data rather than the newer data that had been released on 12 February 2019.
speaker: Democratic Alliance Party

label: Conflicting
claim: Rs. 2000 crore for agri-market infrastructure fund set up
doc: To improve market accessibility and facilitate farmers in directly selling their produce to consumers for better price realization, the Government announced in Union Budget 2018-19 the development and upgrading of existing 22,000 rural haats into Gramin Agricultural Markets (GrAMs). Physical infrastructure in these GrAMs will be strengthened using Government Schemes such as MGNREGA (Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act). These GrAMs are to be exempted from regulations of the Agriculture Produce Marketing Committee (APMCs) and linked to e-NAM to provide farmers with improved market accessibility and facilities to sell their produce at remunerative prices. An Agri-Market Infrastructure Fund with a corpus of Rs. 2,000 crore is targeted to be set up for developing and upgrading agricultural marketing infrastructure in the 22,000 GrAMs, including 585 Agriculture Produce Marketing Committees (APMCs). The Cabinet approved the Agri-Market Infrastructure Fund in February 2019, though the budgetary allocation to the fund remains unclear and the Rs. 2,000 crore represents not the government's budgetary support but rather the overall fund corpus.

label: Conflicting
claim: US chain migration allows a bad person to come into the US, and bring 22 or 23 or 35 of his family members because he has his mother, his grandmother, sister, cousin, uncle.
doc: U.S. citizens and lawful permanent residents can bring certain family members to the United States to live here permanently, though there are significant restrictions on which relatives can be petitioned. Specifically, neither U.S. citizens nor lawful permanent residents can directly petition for an aunt, uncle, cousin, niece, nephew, in-law relative, or grandparent. However, there are theoretical scenarios where such relatives could eventually immigrate. For example, if an immigrant becomes a U.S. citizen and petitions a parent, that parent could eventually become a U.S. citizen and then petition his or her siblings, including aunts and uncles. An immigrant gains the ability to bring in relatives when the person becomes a citizen.
speaker: US President Donald Trump
reporting_source: Press conference at the White House Rose Garden. .

label: Conflicting
claim: The Kenyan government has built a standard-gauge railway of 600 kilometres between 2014 and 2019.
doc: The standard-gauge railway (SGR) has a route length of 472 kilometers and a total track length of 609 kilometers. The difference between these measurements exists because there are areas on the main line with multiple tracks, including two main stations and seven intermediate stations.
speaker: William Ruto

label: Conflicting
claim: The current Kenyan government has constructed 7,000 kilometres of tarmac in the last five years – 12,000 kilometres were constructed in 50 years.
doc: On 8th February 2019, a claim was made regarding Kenya's road infrastructure. According to the 2018 Economic Survey, Kenya had 20,600 km of bitumen roads in 2017. This represented significant growth from 2013, when Kenya had 11,230 kilometres of bitumen roads. President Kenyatta's 2017 election manifesto stated that his administration built 1,950 kilometres of paved road from 2013 to 2017, bringing the total to 13,180 kilometres.
speaker: Kenyan Deputy President, William Ruto

label: Conflicting
claim: Over 700,000 children [accessed] early childhood education in the last financial year
doc: Cyril Ramaphosa significantly underestimated the number of children in early childhood development facilities in South Africa. In 2018, he stated that "nearly one million children" were enrolled in such facilities, and by 2019, he revised this figure to "over 700,000 children." Both estimates were substantially below the actual numbers. While his 2019 statement of "over 700,000" was technically correct in its wording, it remained inaccurate and represented a very low estimate of the true enrollment. According to the 2017 general household survey, just over 2 million children under the age of four were attending early childhood development facilities, including day care centres, crèches, early childhood development centres, playgroups, nursery schools, and preprimary schools. Historical data shows that 2,409,953 children younger than eight were enrolled in some kind of pre-school in 2016, and 1,013,229 children were in pre-school in 2011. Ramaphosa's 2018 claims have been labeled as incorrect, as his suggestion that 1 million children had access to early childhood education significantly underrepresented the actual enrollment figures.
speaker: Cyril Ramaphosa

label: Conflicting
claim: Over 20 percent of Americans between the ages of 25-54 do not have a job, which is higher than was the case 19 years ago.
doc: According to the Bureau of Labor Statistics, the U.S. jobless rate dropped to 3.7 percent in September, representing the lowest level since 1969, despite the economy adding a lower-than-expected 134,000 jobs. The unemployment rate in 2019 was not higher than it had been 20 years prior. In January 2019, 79.9 percent of Americans between the ages of 25 and 54 were working, meaning that 20.1 percent of this population was not employed.
speaker: Warren Gunnels

label: Conflicting
claim: Nigeria's capital expenditure in 2016 was N1.2 trillion and in 2017 was N1.5 trillion.
doc: Nigeria's capital expenditure figures varied across 2016 and 2017 depending on the measurement methodology. In 2016, capital expenditure excluding the share of capital in statutory transfers was recorded at N1.59 trillion, while capital expenditure including the share of capital expenditure in statutory transfers totaled N1.75 trillion. According to the Minister of Finance, the federal government released N1.2 trillion in capital expenses for 2016. In 2017, total capital expenditure reached N2,177,866,775,867 (approximately N2.178 trillion). The Federal Government announced that a total of N1.6 trillion (N1,580,270,755,084.44) in capital costs was released to Ministries, Departments and Agencies for the 2017 federal budget. Minister of Finance Kemi Adeosun noted that the N1.6 trillion total capital releases for 2017 was remarkably higher than the N1.2 trillion (N1,219,471,747,443.00) total capital releases for 2016.
speaker: Peter Obi

label: Conflicting
claim: Since 1994, over 4.7 million free houses have been built, benefiting over 14 million people.
doc: From 1994 to 2018, South Africa constructed 3,263,331 houses. President Kgalema Motlanthe stated that government's social programmes have improved the asset base of the poor through housing, with 2.6 million subsidised houses provided. However, the precise number of people who benefitted from these 3,263,331 homes could not be determined.
speaker: African National Congress

label: Conflicting
claim: Sen. Ted Cruz's 2018 campaign tried to trick elderly Texans with suspicious mailers
doc: During Senator Ted Cruz's 2018 Senate re-election campaign in Texas, his campaign sent out fund-raising letters in envelopes labeled "SUMMONS ENCLOSED — OPEN IMMEDIATELY" in large capital letters, with text in the upper left-hand corner reading "Official Travis County Summons, Voter Enrollment Campaign Division, Ted Cruz for Senate 2018." While the practice drew criticism from some who called it misleading and raised questions about its legality, the letters were not illegal. However, the campaign materials did raise ethical concerns due to the deceptive nature of the envelope labeling, which created confusion between an actual legal summons and a political fund-raising appeal.
speaker: Ted Cruz

label: Conflicting
claim: A man, Emdadur Choudhury, who burned poppies on Remembrance Day 2011 as a counter protest and was fined £50 under the Public Order Act, paid the fine by using his benefits.
doc: On Remembrance Day 2011, a man named Emdadur Choudhury burned poppies and was subsequently fined £50 for his actions. To pay the fine, the extremist revealed that radical Muslim cleric Anjem Choudary had offered to cover the cost. Choudhury was receiving state benefits at the time.
speaker: Albert Gorman

label: Conflicting
claim: Garlic has proven 100 times more effective than antibiotics.
doc: WSU researchers recently reported that diallyl sulfide, a compound found in garlic, is 100 times more effective than the antibiotics erythromycin and ciprofloxacin in killing the toxic bacteria Campylobacter jejuni, the most common cause of food poisoning in the United States. Campylobacter jejuni is particularly difficult to eliminate because it produces a slimy protective biofilm that helps it repel antibiotics and stick to surfaces. Diallyl sulfide works by dissolving this biofilm and killing the bacteria underneath. The mechanism involves diallyl sulfide combining with a sulfur-containing enzyme in the bacteria, which changes the enzyme's function and shuts down cell metabolism, killing bacteria better and faster than antibiotics. Food poisoning from Campylobacter jejuni strikes over 2.4 million Americans each year, causing symptoms including stomach pains, cramping, diarrhea, and fever. While other studies have investigated whether garlic has antiviral properties, the "Garlic for the Common Cold" study was inconclusive.

label: Conflicting
claim: New Zealand’s MPs took a 20% pay cut during this pandemic.
doc: The New Zealand government announced a 20% cut in pay, though Members of Parliament received a reduced cut of 10 per cent.
speaker: Steve Howard

label: Conflicting
claim: Wuhan is where 5G was rolled out first.
doc: Wuhan, the capital of Hubei, was one of the first pilot cities of the 5G network in China. China Mobile, the world's largest mobile operator in terms of subscribers, had plans to carry out external field tests in the cities of Hangzhou, Shanghai, Guangzhou, Suzhou, and Wuhan, deploying more than 100 base stations across these locations. Additionally, China Mobile announced it would conduct 5G network application demonstrations in 12 cities including Beijing, Chengdu, and Shenzhen.

label: Conflicting
claim: Immigrants are 60% less likely to claim benefits than a British-born person.
doc: According to research from the Migration Observatory, immigrants to Britain in 2022 are more likely to claim in-work benefits such as tax credits compared to British-born natives. However, migrants are generally less likely to claim out-of-work benefits than UK-born people.
speaker: Social Media Users

label: Conflicting
claim: Dogs can smell COVID-19 on humans.
doc:
Sniffer dogs can be used to detect COVID-19, and trials have been conducted in Helsinki, Finland and Italy. A research group in France led by veterinary scientist Dominique Grandjean at the National Veterinary School of Alfort near Paris trained 8 dogs to detect COVID-19 in 198 sweat samples, approximately half of which were from people with the disease. When these samples were hidden in a row of negative samples, the dogs identified the positive samples 83–100% of the time, though the paper did not report how well the dogs identified negative test results. The research is currently under review at a journal, though Grandjean notes the publication process has been difficult because most reviewers lack knowledge about working dogs.

While gene-editing scientist Fyodor Urnov at the University of California, Berkeley finds the data promising, he advocates for larger data sets showing how well dogs identify both positive and negative samples. Notably, there is considerable variation in how well individual dogs perform; in Grandjean's study, for example, 2 dogs identified all 68 positive samples, whereas one dog missed 10 out of 57 cases. James Logan, an infectious-disease researcher at the London School of Hygiene & Tropical Medicine who is training and studying COVID-19 detection dogs including Storm, Maple and Asher, agrees that trial groups need to boost their sample sizes before the wider scientific community can properly evaluate how useful the dogs might be. Logan cautions against making grand claims with small data sets prematurely.
speaker: Social Media Users
